A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FLOW and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–I. Content can be matched reliably despite extensive reformatting and table renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original ResNet and language-model fine-tuning experiments, baseline comparisons, and ablations in Sections 5–6 and Appendices H–I.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds ViT-B/16 experiments on Food101, hard-example evaluations, and another temperature sensitivity study.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same fixed exponential weighting of pre-trained losses, weighted fine-tuning, and task-specific head adaptation. The additional architecture and temperature settings are experimental extensions, not changes to FLOW's procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds Food101, extending vision coverage to fine-grained food classification in Appendix H.1. The original six vision datasets, MetaMathQA training, and language evaluation tasks remain.

E2.justification: Learning without Forgetting (LwF; Li and Hoiem, 2016), previously only cited, becomes an evaluated comparator in v2 Table 12. Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds a ViT-B/16 protocol with eight training epochs and FLOW temperature set to the 80th loss percentile, highest-loss 10% evaluations, and a Caltech101 temperature sweep. Its ResNet settings also now exempt linear probing from cosine scheduling. These are reported protocol extensions or revisions; they do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds targeted error analysis on the hardest CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Cars examples (Table 5), plus Caltech101 temperature sensitivity results (Table 11). The existing Cars sensitivity analysis, token-versus-sequence ablation, and weight-averaging analysis remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report seed 42 for the retained language and ResNet experiments and present point estimates. V2 introduces no repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–4 retain their numerical results. V2 adds results in Tables 5, 11, and 12, including Food101 average accuracy of 84.26 for FLOW versus 83.81 for LwF. It also corrects Gemma standard-fine-tuning HellaSwag from 45.59 to 54.41 and PIQA from 9.76 to 76.99 in v1 Table 10 versus v2 Table 13, matching values already reported in v1's token-weighting table.

T1.justification: The formal assumptions, weighting derivation, Proposition 4.3, Theorem 7.2, and supporting proofs in Appendices C–F are substantively unchanged. Condensed notation and relocated explanations do not change the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and concluding summary retain the same central claims: loss-based weighting mitigates forgetting without pre-training data, complements existing methods, and stalls learning along particular directions in the linear analysis.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly attributes the retention tradeoff to poorer performance on hard examples and discusses improving that failure mode and extending the linear theory. Appendix A additionally discusses possible factuality and soft-unlearning applications; these are proposed connections, not demonstrated capabilities.

D1.justification: Appendix G adds ViT learning rates and LwF settings, including temperature 2 and distillation coefficient 5e-4. The expanded ResNet hyperparameter table supplies missing dataset column labels, but v1's explicit zero-weight-decay exception for the regularization baseline is no longer documented. The same code link is retained in a relocated footnote.

R1.justification: V2 adds four references covering Food101, ViT, and factuality research by Ghosal et al. and Gekhman et al.; no cited works are removed. It expands positioning through factuality/unlearning connections and a more explicit comparison with LwF, while retaining the existing related-work survey.

P1.justification: The narrative and section order largely remain intact. Local edits add a limitations discussion, application discussion, a distillation-comparison subsection, and an impact statement, alongside revised headings, author information, and acknowledgments.

P2.justification: V2 substantially redesigns presentation using a two-column conference layout for the main text and references, with changed typography and resized or repositioned displays. It adds three tables and expands the vision hyperparameter table; the four original figures remain.

improvement.justification: The added LwF comparison, explicit hard-example failure analysis, and repaired appendix entries make the evidence more informative and the limitations clearer. Gains are limited: the core method and main results remain unchanged, and the new Caltech101 temperature sweep is not reconciled with the retained Caltech101 scores in Tables 9–10.
